title: Validator-metric suite for measuring soundness, coverage, and operational impact of GVR oracles in NetOps
research_question: Can a standardized, empirically estimable validator metric suite (coverage, FP-rate, FN-rate, mean detection latency, operational-impact score) predict end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single raw verifier pass rate?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: A multi-dimensional validator metric suite explains more variance in end-to-end task success than a single verifier pass rate (primary confirmatory hypothesis).
H2: Injected, preregistered realistic fault classes permit stable estimation of validator false-negative and false-positive rates under the controlled benchmark.
H3: Validator metrics correlate with a preregistered simulated operational-impact cost proxy and can be used to prioritize verifier development.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: Which injected fault classes (syntactic, semantic, configuration-logic, policy-violation) most strongly drive false-negative/false-positive tradeoffs?
EQ2: How sensitive are validator-metric estimates and predictive performance to alternative operational-cost parameterizations?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic paired NetOps GVR episodes generated via the supplied synthetic_paired_llm_benchmark_v1 / hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family.
Stress-test task-index profile: challenging_workflow_stress_v1 (only 'very_hard' and 'extreme' generator levels) as required by the adapter contract.
model_scope: Single hosted LLM accessed via hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (provider-model name/version to be recorded in execution manifest).
No private vendor-only verifiers; only public/open-source deterministic validators or deterministic checks embedded in scoring scripts.
transformation_scope: baseline: direct_configuration_generation_v1 (one generation call per task).
guarded: generate_validate_repair_v1 (initial generation + at most one repair call per task, as per adapter contract).
secondary_estimands: per-validator false-positive rate (FP-rate) averaged across tasks
per-validator false-negative rate (FN-rate) averaged across tasks
R^2 of linear model predicting simulated operational-impact score from validator metric vectors
sampling_plan: Confirmatory paired design using hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter with episodes_per_task=2 (baseline, guarded). Task selection: deterministic challenging_workflow_stress_v1 profile (adapter-prescribed index rule). Three preplanned scenarios (minimal/recommended/ambitious). For the recommended (primary) scenario: task_count = 200 tasks. Derivation: adapter requires 1 initial generation and up to 1 repair call per task → maximum_model_calls = task_count * 2 = 200 * 2 = 400 model calls. Episodes: 2 per task → 400 episodes total (200 baseline, 200 guarded). All selection and indices fixed before any hosted-model call.
analysis_plan: Primary confirmatory analysis executed by 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' executor (available). Estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Primary test: paired two-condition difference in binary success (guarded vs baseline) using the executor's permutation / paired-proportion test. Report estimate, 95% CI, and p-value. Model-failure handling per adapter/contract: follow failed_call_treatment=['complete_pair_primary','complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity'] — primary analysis uses complete pairs only; sensitivity analysis treats any incomplete pair as failure (0) for guarded condition. Secondary analyses: linear regression (or robust regression) predicting simulated operational-impact score from validator metric vectors; report adjusted R^2 and AUC for binary impact-thresholded outcomes. Bootstrap (1,000 resamples) for stability of metric estimates and predictive statistics. All analysis code and executor configuration will be published with artifacts.
multiplicity_plan: Single pre-registered primary confirmatory estimand (paired success-rate difference). All subgroup, per-error-class, per-validator, and cost-parameter analyses are explicitly exploratory and will use false-discovery-rate control (Benjamini–Hochberg) when reporting multiple p-values, or will be reported with effect sizes and confidence intervals without formal multiplicity claims for hypothesis testing.
missingness_plan: API/infrastructure failures: no manual retries beyond adapter limits (maximum_attempts_per_call=1). Primary analysis uses complete pairs only (executor default). Sensitivity analysis treats missing/failed episodes as failures (0). All missingness, retry, and failure metadata (timestamps, HTTP codes, provider error messages) logged in execution manifest. No human adjudication will be used to impute missingness.

risk_factors: Task-generator leakage between training and evaluation regimes (generator producing trivial or out-of-scope prompts).
Duplicate or near-duplicate seeded outputs across tasks.
Validator implementations sharing code/heuristics with generation templates causing optimistic validator coverage estimates.
detection_procedures: Deterministic duplicate-detection on task and generated-output hashes (SHA-256) and automatic exclusion of exact duplicates from analyses.

Automated semantic-similarity screening (embedding cosine similarity threshold) to flag near-duplicate tasks; flagged items are excluded from confirmatory sample if similarity > 0.95 (deterministic rule).
Run validators against a held-out set of clean, non-seeded generator outputs to detect validator overfitting to seeded templates (automatic comparison of FP/FN rates).
item_flagging_rules: Exact-duplicate outputs (identical SHA-256) → automatic exclusion from confirmatory set and logging as contamination-exclusion.
Near-duplicate tasks (embedding similarity > 0.95) → deterministic exclusion; replacement follow deterministic next-index rule to preserve task_count.

Validator-overfitting signal (large FP/FN divergence between seeded and held-out generator set, preregistered threshold: >20 percentage points) → automatic relegation of affected validator to exploratory-only analyses.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Confirmatory analyses run on contamination-cleaned dataset per deterministic exclusion rules. All exclusions, replacements, and contamination logs are published alongside raw artifacts. Sensitivity analyses will report results both including and excluding flagged items.
residual_uncertainty: Seeded taxonomy coverage vs real-world error distributions (bounded in remaining_noncritical_uncertainties).
Potential unseen generator–validator coupling beyond automated detection heuristics.

budget_scenarios.description: Minimal confirmatory run to verify pipeline and estimate variance (fast sanity-check).
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 100 tasks × up to 2 calls/task = 200 model calls. Fits well under model-call budget (<=10000) and enables quick pipeline validation; lower statistical power than recommended scenario.

budget_scenarios.description: Primary recommended confirmatory run balancing power and cost.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 200 tasks × up to 2 calls/task = 400 model calls. Within manifest limits; provides sufficient sample to detect ~10 percentage-point paired differences under preregistered assumptions (see power_plan).

budget_scenarios.description: Ambitious run to increase sensitivity for subgroup and per-error-class analyses.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 500 tasks × up to 2 calls/task = 1000 model calls. Still within the manifest model-call budget and execution window but requires longer runtime and more storage; exploratory subgroup estimates improve with this sample.

power_plan.target_effect: Detect an absolute paired improvement of 0.10 (10 percentage points) in success rate (guarded minus baseline) with alpha=0.05 (two-sided) and ~80% power under conservative assumptions.
power_plan.clustering_unit: task (paired episodes per task: baseline + guarded)
power_plan.calculation_method: Approximate normal/paired-proportion calculation under conservative baseline p=0.50 and zero within-pair correlation for MDE approximation; bootstrap stability checks (1,000 resamples) to account for distributional deviations.
assumptions: Within-pair correlation modest; MDE calculations presented for correlation=0 and sensitivity analyses for correlations in [0,0.3].
No post-hoc sample changes; all task indices fixed a priori.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With n=200 paired tasks, approximate standard error for a 0.5 baseline yields SE≈0.05, giving a 95% CI half-width ≈0.10; thus ~10 percentage points is a conservative detectable difference. Sensitivity analyses will compute MDE over plausible baseline rates (0.3–0.7) and correlations.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute MDE for baseline p in {0.3,0.4,0.5,0.6,0.7}.
Recompute power under within-pair correlations ρ in {0,0.1,0.2,0.3}.
Report bootstrap-derived empirical SE and MDE from pilot minimal scenario (scenario_minimal_100) if that run is executed first.

semantic_equivalence_checks: Automated token-level and semantic-similarity checks between repaired and intended-configuration specifications (embedding similarity thresholds and deterministic rule checks for preserved intent tokens).

Deterministic mapping checks ensuring that guarded repairs do not change intent keywords defined in the task prompt; any repair that alters intent keywords is flagged and excluded from the primary confirmatory success metric (documented deterministic rule).
automatic_rejection_rules: Repaired configurations that omit any preregistered mandatory parameters (deterministic rule) → automatic failure for that episode.
Repairs that introduce network-actions outside the task's allowed action set (predeclared per-task) → automatic exclusion from primary success numerator and logging as policy-violation repairs.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Deterministic cryptographic sampling: select the first 20 tasks by task_index for extra telemetry logging and archival of full validator traces; no human audit required — all traces are stored and published.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Publish all mapping rules used to translate generator outputs to validator input formats; include unit tests (deterministic) in released scoring scripts.
residual_risks: Semantic-equivalence checks are heuristic and may miss subtle intent drift.
Deterministic exclusion rules may bias the confirmatory sample if many exclusions occur; this will be reported and sensitivity-analysed.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Representativeness of the seeded-fault taxonomy for real-world operational error distributions; claims explicitly bounded to the seeded taxonomy.
Detection-latency estimates may be sensitive to hosted-model API latency variation and infrastructure jitter; we mitigate via repeated time measurements and by reporting median and IQR.
Single-hosted-LLM execution limits generalization across model vendors; claims restricted to the tested model and the synthetic benchmark population.
